planner.question: Can a fixed input-dependent two-order verifier family repair the previous nonuniform transfer quantifier, and can any occurrence layout make its frontier small?
planner.strategy: Construct one universal clause-pool program and prove a layout-independent frontier lower bound.
planner.alternative: Count distinct deterministic residual functions in a units-first selector order.
planner.stop_rule: Do not equate an exponential explicit state domain or ordered branching program bound with general circuit hardness.
literature_leads: Prior MathOS witness-pass frontier and bounded reflection clause pools; standard cutwidth subset DP and residual-function counting. No novelty claim.

construct.claim: The fixed selector-dependent width-three two-pass family computes 3SAT, with minimum occurrence frontier Theta(n) over every layout.
construct.scope: Full normalized nonempty width-three pool; within-variable second-pass order follows first-pass order; multiedges counted.
construct.derivation: Clause selectors gate local checks, repeated occurrences enforce equality; cut before last variable group is touched has n-1 distinct crossings.
unresolved_steps: Polynomial deterministic circuits for the universal family or a lower bound covering general circuits.
candidate_tests: Compile fixed pools once for all selectors; compare exact source and occurrence witnesses; compute small optimal layouts.

alternative.claim: Every deterministic ordered read-once selector program with units first requires at least 2^n states after the unit block.
alternative.scope: Full selector pool, n>=2, fixed units-first order.
alternative.derivation: Unit prefixes force distinct assignments; a remaining binary clause distinguishes any pair of residual functions.
unresolved_steps: Arbitrary orders, adaptive repeated queries and general circuits.
candidate_tests: Enumerate all signed binary residual signatures and pairwise distinctions.
